title: The Sermon at Benares
book: NCERT First Flight: Textbook in English for Class X
subject: english_literature
author: Betty Renshaw
syllabus_note: CBSE 2025-26 English Language and Literature (184): First Flight prose, Chapter 8. Assessed through extracts (5 marks), short answers in 40-50 words (3 marks) and long answers in 100-120 words (6 marks).

blocks.title: A handful of mustard seed
blocks.body:
A young mother's only son dies. Mad with grief, she goes from house to house begging for medicine to bring him back. A wise man says he can help, if she brings him a handful of **mustard seed** from a house where **no one has ever died**.

In this chapter we learn about the life of **Gautama Buddha** and how he taught Kisa Gotami, and all of us, to understand death and grief.

blocks.title: The writer
blocks.body: The chapter, retold by **Betty Renshaw**, presents the life of the Buddha and his first sermon at **Benares** (Varanasi). The story of **Kisa Gotami** is one of the best-known Buddhist parables about accepting death.
blocks.future: Counsellors, doctors and teachers help people cope with grief; understanding loss is part of growing up.

blocks.question: Why did the Buddha send Kisa Gotami for mustard seed instead of simply telling her that death is certain?
options: So that she would discover for herself that every family has suffered death
To keep her busy and forget her son
blocks.explanation: Truth we discover ourselves stays with us longer.

blocks.title: From prince to the Enlightened One
blocks.body:
**Gautama Buddha (563 B.C. – 483 B.C.)** began life as **Prince Siddhartha Gautama** in northern India. At **twelve** he was sent away for schooling in the Hindu sacred scriptures, and four years later he returned home to **marry a princess**. They had a son and lived for **ten years** as befitted royalty.

At about the age of **twenty-five**, the prince, who had been shielded from the sufferings of the world, while out hunting saw a **sick man**, then an **aged man**, then a **funeral procession**, and finally a **monk begging for alms**. These sights moved him so much that he went out into the world to seek **enlightenment** concerning the sorrows he had witnessed.

He wandered for **seven years** and finally sat down under a **peepal tree**, vowing to stay there until enlightenment came. Enlightened after **seven days**, he renamed the tree the **Bodhi Tree** (Tree of Wisdom) and began to teach and share his new understanding. He became known as **the Buddha** (the Awakened or the Enlightened). He preached his **first sermon** at the city of **Benares**, most holy of the dipping places on the river Ganges.

blocks.title: The Buddha's life at a glance
blocks.body:
| Stage | What happened |
|---|---|
| **Birth** | born Prince Siddhartha Gautama in northern India (563 B.C.) |
| **Age 12** | sent away to study the Hindu sacred scriptures |
| **Four years later** | returned home, married a princess, had a son; lived ten years as a royal prince |
| **About 25** | saw a sick man, an aged man, a funeral procession and a monk begging for alms |
| **Seven years** | wandered in search of enlightenment |
| **Under the peepal tree** | sat until enlightened after seven days; named it the **Bodhi Tree** (Tree of Wisdom); became the **Buddha** (the Awakened or Enlightened) |
| **Benares** | preached his first sermon at Benares, the holiest dipping place on the Ganges |

blocks.question: Which sights changed Prince Siddhartha's life?
options: a sick man, an aged man, a funeral procession and a monk begging for alms
blocks.explanation: He had been shielded from the world's sufferings until then.

blocks.question: What does 'Buddha' mean?
blocks.explanation: He gained enlightenment under the Bodhi Tree.

blocks.title: The mustard seed and the lesson
blocks.body:
**Kisa Gotami's grief:** Kisa Gotami had an only son, and he died. In her grief she carried the dead child to all her neighbours, asking them for **medicine**. People said, 'She has lost her senses. The boy is dead.' At last a man said, 'I cannot give thee medicine for thy child, but I know a physician who can,' and directed her to **Sakyamuni, the Buddha**.

**The test:** the Buddha asked for **a handful of mustard seed**, but it must be taken from a house where **no one had lost a child, husband, parent or friend**. Kisa Gotami went from house to house. Everyone pitied her and was ready to give seed, but in every house someone had died: 'The living are few, but the dead are many.'

**Understanding:** weary and hopeless, she sat down at the wayside, watching the lights of the city as they **flickered up and were extinguished** again. She thought, 'How selfish am I in my grief! **Death is common to all**; yet in this valley of desolation there is a path that leads him to immortality who has surrendered all selfishness.'

**The sermon:** the Buddha said: the life of mortals is **troubled and brief and combined with pain**. As **ripe fruits** are early in danger of falling, so mortals when born are always in danger of death. As all **earthen vessels** made by the potter end in being broken, so is the life of mortals. Not from weeping nor from grieving will anyone obtain peace of mind; it only brings more pain. He who has **drawn out the arrow** of lamentation and grief will obtain peace of mind; he who has overcome all sorrow will become **free from sorrow, and be blessed**.

blocks.question: What condition did the Buddha put on the mustard seed?
options: it must come from a house where no one had lost a child, husband, parent or friend
it must be bought with money
it must come from a temple
option_feedback: It was about death in the house.
It was about death in the house.

blocks.question: What did Kisa Gotami understand at last?
options: death is common to all, and she was selfish in her grief
blocks.explanation: She watched the city lights flicker and go out.

blocks.title: Words, images and comparisons
blocks.body:
| Word or phrase | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **enlightenment** | spiritual wisdom and understanding |
| **alms** | money or food given to the poor |
| **sermon** | a religious talk |
| **mortals** | human beings, who must die |
| **desolation** | great sadness and emptiness |
| **lamentation** | crying aloud in grief |
| **Sakyamuni** | 'sage of the Sakyas', a name of the Buddha |

**Similes in the sermon:** life is like **ripe fruit** that may fall early; like **earthen vessels** that end in being broken. **Image:** the city lights flickering up and going out show that lives begin and end. **Metaphor:** grief is an **arrow** to be drawn out.

blocks.question: What do the flickering city lights symbolise?
options: human lives that begin and end
blocks.explanation: This image helps Kisa Gotami understand.

blocks.title: Memory tricks
blocks.body:
- **Four sights: Sick, Old, Dead, Monk ("SODM").**
- **Numbers: 12 school, +4 married, 10 royal years, ~25 sights, 7 years wandering, 7 days under the tree.**
- **Sermon images: ripe fruit, earthen pots, arrow of grief.**
- **Kisa's realisation: 'The living are few, but the dead are many.'**

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.body:
1. Saying the Buddha brought the child back to life: he taught Kisa to **accept** death.
2. Writing that the first sermon was at Bodh Gaya: enlightenment was under the Bodhi Tree; the first sermon was at **Benares**.
3. Saying Kisa got mustard seed: she could not find a house without death, which was the lesson.
4. Mixing up 'alms' (charity) and 'arms'.

blocks.title: Try this in class
blocks.body: Compare Kisa Gotami's first and second searches: what she wanted, whom she met, what she learnt. Students fill a two-column chart.

blocks.title: Think and explain
blocks.body: How can we comfort a friend who has lost someone dear? What would the Buddha's lesson suggest?

blocks.title: Where this leads
blocks.body:
- **Madam Rides the Bus (Ch 7) and The Ball Poem:** first lessons in loss.
- **History:** Buddhism spread across Asia; India's state emblem comes from Ashoka's pillar at Sarnath, near Benares, where the first sermon was given.

blocks.title: Mastery challenge
blocks.body:
How did the Buddha help Kisa Gotami overcome her grief? Answer in about 120 words.

**Model answer:** When Kisa Gotami's only son died, she was so lost in grief that she carried his body from house to house asking for medicine. The Buddha did not lecture her. Instead he asked her to bring a handful of mustard seed from a house where no one had lost a child, husband, parent or friend. In every house she found that someone had died, and she realised that 'the living are few, but the dead are many'. Watching the city lights flicker and go out, she understood that death is common to all and that her grief had been selfish. The Buddha then taught that grieving only brings more pain, and that one who overcomes sorrow finds peace. By letting her discover the truth herself, he healed her.

blocks.title: Chapter summary
blocks.body:
- Prince Siddhartha, moved by the sight of sickness, old age, death and a monk, left his royal life to seek enlightenment.
- After seven years of wandering he was enlightened under the Bodhi Tree and became the Buddha; he preached his first sermon at Benares.
- Kisa Gotami, grieving for her dead son, was asked to bring mustard seed from a house untouched by death; she found none and understood that death is universal.
- The Buddha taught that weeping brings no peace; overcoming sorrow brings peace and blessing.

blocks.title: Exam tips
blocks.body:
- Use the two comparisons from the sermon (ripe fruit, earthen vessels) in answers on the nature of life.
- Compare Kisa's two searches when asked how she changed.
- Value-based long answers: link the lesson to coping with loss today.
